data.title: How Market Payments and Member Services Work Today

questions.tip: Ask for the most recent real example, including who paid whom and when.
questions.question: Tell me about the last market trade you completed and how the payment was settled.

questions.tip: Listen for actual settlement times, delays, and steps rather than general opinions.
questions.question: What usually happens between completing a trade and receiving the money?

questions.tip: Ask what happened next and what it cost in time, money, or trust.
questions.question: Tell me about the last time a delayed payment caused a problem for you or your members.

questions.tip: Explore workarounds already used and what the person paid for them.
questions.question: What have you done in the past to receive or send payment sooner?

questions.tip: Ask how much they paid, why they paid, and what made the cost worthwhile.
questions.question: Tell me about the last financial service or payment service you paid to use.

questions.tip: Ask for examples of that decision, not what they would do in theory.
questions.question: How do you decide whether a payment service is worth paying for?

questions.tip: Ask what the association did, why it recommended it, and what members did afterward.
questions.question: Tell me about the last time your market association recommended a product or service to members.

questions.tip: Look for evidence of past promotion, member response, and any money or effort involved.
questions.question: What services has your association promoted or arranged for members in the past year?

questions.tip: Ask how the association responded and what happened after the response.
questions.question: Tell me about a time members asked the association to help solve a payment or settlement problem.
